as_told.title: Rumored 2004 dogfight between Lockheed and JSOC crash retrieval teams

plain: Two teams are said to have reached the same crashed craft at once and shot at each other. One was a private military crew working under contract for Lockheed Martin. The other came from JSOC, the Joint Special Operations Command, which runs the US military's most secretive special forces units. Michels's co-host, a defence and aerospace engineer who goes by the pseudonym Jack and has more than 15 years in the field, brings it up while interviewing a guest. He calls it "a story" that a contractor was "sent out to recover a crash" and that the JSOC team was "sent out to the same crash site." Michels tells it again in a later episode as a rumour of "a dog fight" between the two retrieval teams. He gives more detail than Jack: he dates it to 2004, sets it at Coyame, Mexico, and ties it to a man named Jake Barber and to a work called Sentinels of Ether that he links to Barber. If it were true, it would mean rival groups inside the American system were racing each other for crashed craft.
